chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Safwan from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"If a man has intercourse with his wife before reaching al-Muzdalifah or before he arrives at al-Muzdalifah, then upon him is the Hajj of next year." And the meaning of what has preceded from these narrations, that they are distinguished and do not combine, is that they are not empty except that with them is the other, and that which indicates this is what was narrated:

key_terms.الْحَجُّ مِنْ قَابِلٍ: The Hajj of the following year, a specific expiation for this ritual error
key_terms.الْمُزْدَلِفَة: Muzdalifah, a sacred site in Mecca where pilgrims gather after standing at Arafat
key_terms.يُفَرَّقُ بَيْنَهُمَا: They are distinguished/separated, referring to distinguishing between different legal rulings or narrations

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for having sexual intercourse with one's wife before reaching Muzdalifah during Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* specifies that sexual intercourse before reaching al-Muzdalifah invalidates the current Hajj, requiring a fresh performance the following year, a ruling distinct from the expiation (*kaffarah*) applicable to other breaches. The text clarifies that this specific penalty applies exclusively to this timing, distinguishing it from other narrations where intercourse might incur a different penalty or be combined with other conditions. This highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on precise timing in determining the severity of ritual violations during the Hajj rites.
